143	
144	**2.6 One writer, enforced.** Only `PipelineRoot` (and its `ViewportWiring` helper, `src/presentation/pipeline/viewport_wiring.gd`) may write: `SubViewport.size`, `size_2d_override*`, the container's `position`, `scale`, `stretch_shrink` and `material`, any `CanvasLayer.scale` / `offset` / `transform`, `HudRoot.size`; the world viewport's `canvas_transform` and the parallax layer offsets are written only by the **`CameraHost`'s `frame_pre_draw` handler** (§ 6.2). These two are the geometry writers named on ADR-0009's lint allow-list; they are legitimate and do not go through `Placement` (parallax offsets still use `Placement`'s integer helpers). Presentation subscribers (the Filter, Lighting, HUD, Chart Table) call neither; they receive a read-only `RenderLayout` (§ 3) and `world_to_hud`.
145	
146	### 3. Geometry: `k`, `H`, aspect, zoom, and one `RESCALING` path
147	
148	**Decision.** All derived geometry is one **pure function**, `RenderLayout.derive(...)`, a `RefCounted` value with no scene-tree dependency, injected where read. It implements the GDD's Formulas D.1 to D.5 and D.14 as written (the GDD owns the formulas; this ADR owns where their outputs go). `PipelineRoot` is the only caller that applies a result.
149	
150	- **Inputs:** the window pixel size `W x H_w` (physical pixels, never DPI-scaled; `content_scale_factor` stays 1.0), a `DisplaySettings` value (aspect `KEEP | EXPAND`, manual world scale `0` for Auto, HUD scale choice), the current zoom step `k_z`, the static `ZOOM_MIN_K` row table (carried by `RenderTuning`, § 6.1), and the `offered(P_w, P_h)` subset of HUD scales from `HudLayout` (HUD owns the predicate `bottom_row_fit`). `offered_h` is an `Array[int]` that `derive` duplicates on entry, so a caller that mutates it afterwards, or a layout that keeps it, cannot change a result.
151	- **Outputs (all integers or integer-valued):** `k_auto = floor(min(W/640, H_w/360))` (a window below `min_size` 1280x720 cannot occur on a compliant window manager; if one does, `k_auto` is clamped to the Section G invariant `k_min == 2` and a `WINDOW_BELOW_MIN` diagnostics entry is written, never a `k` of 1 or 0), `k_base` (manual `k` when below Auto, else `k_auto`; a manual `k` below Auto forces `KEEP`), `H` (`H_default = max(k_auto, 3)`, never below 3, in `[H_default, 2 * H_default]` and in `offered`), `field_px` (D.1/D.3 at `k_base`, D.5 at a ladder step), `picture_rect` (the window region that shows the game, centred, integer), `world_rect = field_px * k_z` centred in the picture (a ladder field that does not divide the picture leaves a few black pixels; the HUD does not move), `hud_rect` (**pinned to the `k_base` picture rect**, so a zoom step never moves the HUD), `hud_canvas = hud_rect.size / H`.
152	- **Letterbox bars** are the root viewport's **clear colour** (`default_clear_color = (0,0,0,1)`, § 5.1), outside every node, so the Filter, the jolt and any `CanvasLayer` cannot touch them. A 1-HUD-px hairline at the picture edge, if the art director adds one, is a layer-1 element excluded from the HUD count (PR-12 resolution).
153	
154	**3.1 Zoom is a change of logical size, never `Camera2D.zoom`.** The ladder is `[effective_min, k_base + 2]` with `effective_min = ZOOM_MIN_K(k_base, target class)` (default 1 until the spike fills it); `k_z` is persistent, edge-triggered, never held and never saved. `PipelineRoot.request_zoom_step(direction: int)` is the only entry point (the Input Adapter calls it from its `_process`; ADR-0019). A step is accepted when it is inside the ladder, no other step was accepted this frame, and at least `ZOOM_STEP_MIN_INTERVAL` (0.15 s) of **engine process time** has passed since the last accepted step; the interval is a countdown decremented by the `_process` delta divided by `Engine.time_scale` (guarded when the scale is 0) in `PipelineRoot`, so the cooldown is wall-clock even if `time_scale` is not 1 (whether `time_scale` scales `delta` is UNVERIFIED in ADR-0001; the injected monotonic `Clock` of ADR-0010 is an equivalent source and either satisfies the rule), **not** `present_time` (frozen under pause, where zoom must still work) and not any `Time.*` call (forbidden by ADR-0001's clock lint); surplus presses are discarded, not queued, and counted in `diag.zoom_step_rate_limited`. A refused press (beyond either end, or below `ZOOM_MIN_K`, or while the camera is `HELD`) increments `diag.zoom_step_refused` with a reason. Accepting a step sets the layout dirty, so the step is **one `RESCALING` frame and a camera cut**: under pass A `SubViewport.size = field_px(k_z)` and `container.scale = k_z`; under pass B `size = field_px * k_z`, `override = field_px`. Lighting has no zoom handler: every `Light2D` length is in base px and independent of `k_z` under both passes (LO-16), which this wiring honours because the world canvas is never scaled by `Camera2D`.
155	
156	**3.2 One `RESCALING` path for every cause.** `Window.size_changed`, a zoom step, a display-mode change, a world-scale or HUD-scale or aspect setting change, and `dpi_changed` each **only set a dirty flag** (the same dirty-mark principle as every notification). `PipelineRoot._process` is the single presentation entry point; it does the following **in this fixed order inside one function** (no priority tie, no tree-order dependency):
157	1. advance `present_time` (§ 6.3);
158	2. decrement the zoom cooldown (§ 3.1);
159	3. if the layout is dirty, run `RESCALING` (below);
160	4. call `driver.frame(delta, present_time)`, which runs ADR-0009's stages in order, `CAMERA_SOLVE` first (§ 6.2).
161	
162	The re-derivation therefore happens at most once per rendered frame and completes before any presenter of that frame draws (the main loop processes events, then `_process`, then draws), so a continuous drag of the window edge is a sequence of at most one re-derivation per frame converging on the final size (coalescing by frame, not by time). `RESCALING`:
163	1. computes the new `RenderLayout`;
164	2. **reallocates the viewport only if `field_px`, `k_z` or the render mode's size changed**; a pure translation (the picture re-centring by a pixel during a drag) moves only the container position and the HUD rect;
165	3. applies it through `ViewportWiring` (container position and scale, viewport size and override, layer offsets and scales, `HudRoot.size`), calls `HudLayout` once, re-derives the camera limits rectangle consumed by the solver, increments the layout version counter that `PipelineRoot` holds (consumers poll it), and republishes `world_to_hud`'s inputs;
166	4. sets `UPDATE_ONCE` on the frame of any size change while updates are disabled (**mandatory**, not a guard: a resize of a disabled viewport clears it, § 2.2), then `PipelineRoot` sets `UPDATE_DISABLED` itself on the next frame;
167	5. enters the `RESCALING` state for that frame and `PRESENTING` (or the held state) on the next.
168	
169	The re-derivation completes inside the frame and costs at most 4 ms CPU (§ 7). No frame shows a fractional transform because there is none to show: every transform written is integer-valued. Code that runs right after a resize must not read `WorldContainer.size` or mouse rects: the container is a `Control` under a non-`Control` parent, its `size` refreshes from the viewport's minimum size at the next deferred update and is stale until then (drawing is unaffected with `stretch = false`); only `scale` and `position`, which the pipeline itself wrote, are read (§ Implementation Guidelines, Gotchas).

235	### 6. The presentation host, the camera solve and write, and `present_time`
236	
237	**6.1 The camera is a pure solver run in the `CAMERA_SOLVE` stage (TR-pxl-010, 011, 012, 013, 015; the formulas D.6 to D.10 are the GDD's).** `CameraSolver` is a `RefCounted` with `solve(input: SolverInput, state: SolverState, params: SolverParams) -> Pose`, no scene-tree dependency, float64 per-axis state held as scalars (not `Vector2`), `dt` clamped to `DT_MAX` (0.05 s). The **type of `SolverInput` is the enforcement of Camera C1**: it carries only the follow target's previous and current body-local positions, `tick_alpha`, the raw local beam aim, the zoom step, `dt`, and cut / rebase flags; it has no field through which Attention, breach, horrors, sound, the graph or sanity could enter, so the same input trace gives the same camera trace in calm, tell and breach by construction. The Perception Filter has no write path to a camera or viewport property (§ 2.6). The camera is a `PresenterDescriptor` registered at `PresentationStage.CAMERA_SOLVE` (stage 1, ADR-0009 § 3): it calls `solve` once per frame from `driver.frame` and **publishes `pose_q`, the follow pose `f_q`, the jolt offset, the parallax offsets and the `world_to_hud` inputs** to `CameraHost` and `RenderLayout` before the Avatar, Filter, HUD and Lighting stages run. Solver parameters (`tau_follow`, `DT_MAX`) and `ZOOM_MIN_K` are the `RenderTuning` table loaded by ADR-0007's pipeline and injected (schema in Key Interfaces). Camera state is never persisted.
238	
239	*Restore and discontinuity.* The kernel calls `snap_baseline` on every interpolated block on each transition into `RUNNING` (ADR-0001 § 4, ADR-0003), so the first frame after a restore interpolates nothing; that is the **only** restore-continuity mechanism and this ADR adds no owner-side rule. The camera stage additionally **CUTs** the solver (starting with `L = 0` easing in) in its `on_discontinuity(DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE)`, which ADR-0009's driver delivers when `PresentationClock.load_seq` changes (the kernel increments it on every `LOADING → RUNNING` transition, restore and new game, never on `PAUSED` or `SAVING → RUNNING`; ADR-0001 amendment batch). A pod or transit body transfer is a CUT; a weld or detach `BODY_TRANSFER` carrying `frame_delta_px` calls `rebase(frame_delta_px)`, which shifts the follow and history and keeps lag and `L`.
240	
241	**6.2 The frame model and the hook.** `PipelineRoot` **is** ADR-0009's single `PresentationHost` (closing ADR-0009 OQ-E, OQ-J and OQ-L): no other node hosts the driver, and because every step below runs inside one function, no priority tie and no tree-order dependency exists. The composition root constructs the `PresentationDriver` and injects it; `PipelineRoot` holds it. Its single `_process`, at `ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION`, runs in this fixed order: (1) advance `present_time` (§ 6.3); (2) the zoom cooldown (§ 3.1); (3) the `RESCALING` re-derive if dirty (§ 3.2); (4) `driver.frame(delta, present_time)`, which runs the stages with `CAMERA_SOLVE` first. Presenters have no `_process`; **there are no subscribers drawing from their own `_process`** (ADR-0009 Alternatives 1 and 2 reject that shape).
242	
243	The `CameraHost` (a top-level presentation node under `PipelineRoot`, never a child of a body) connects one handler to **`RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw`**. The handler does exactly two writes from already-solved values and nothing else: the world viewport's `canvas_transform` (from `pose_q` plus the jolt offset) and the parallax layer offsets (integer offsets the camera stage computed with `Placement`'s integer helpers, `floori`, not a bare `-floor(...)`). It **does not solve**, it is **idempotent and branch-free**, and it is **safe if the handler is skipped for a frame** (a minimised or occluded window): the next call writes the then-current solved values and nothing accumulates. **Primary variant: no `Camera2D` in the world tree** (a lint); the transform has scale (1,1), no rotation and no skew every frame and only the host writes it. **Alternative variant**, if the direct write is rejected at step 12: a `Camera2D` with `anchor_mode = ANCHOR_MODE_FIXED_TOP_LEFT` (probed: `anchor_mode` default 1 is `DRAG_CENTER`), drag margins off, and `force_update_scroll()` called after each write; every camera assertion is read as holding on the `Camera2D` if the variant has one. `Camera2D.limit_*` stays at the engine defaults in both variants; **the solver is the only clamp** against the limits rectangle a PROJECTOR sets (ADR-0034), so `world_to_hud` is never offset while `CLAMPED`. Solving in the `_process` pass also keeps the solver unit-testable without a signal that never fires headless.

## Decision

Five numbered sub-decisions, each reviewable alone: **§ 1 renderer method and Windows driver**, **§ 2 the viewport stack and scale wiring**, **§ 3 geometry, `k`, `H`, aspect and zoom**, **§ 4 render mode A and B**, **§ 5 project pins and startup guard rails**. Two shorter ones follow because other ADRs cite them: **§ 6 the presentation host, the camera solve and write, and `present_time`**, and **§ 7 the draw-call and timing budget rules**.

### 1. Renderer method and Windows driver

**Decision (provisional, pinned, spike-reversible).**
- **Method: Forward+** (`rendering/renderer/rendering_method = "forward_plus"`, already in `project.godot`). Compatibility and Mobile are assumed nowhere.
- **Windows driver: Vulkan** (`rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows = "vulkan"`), and the Linux / Steam Deck driver is Vulkan (`driver.linuxbsd = "vulkan"`). Direct3D 12 is the recorded alternative.
- **The driver is never left to the engine default.** Windowed probe on 4.7.2: a project with no driver key reports `vulkan` / `forward_plus`, and the `ProjectSettings` default of `driver.windows` is `vulkan` (`driver.linuxbsd` `vulkan`, `driver.macos` `metal`); the reference's "D3D12 is the Windows default since 4.6" is therefore not what a key-absent project gets and is most plausibly a new-project-template value (UNVERIFIED, OQ-C). Either could be the value a later 4.7.x patch or a template re-save writes, and the editor drops a key whose value equals its default, so the key may be absent from `project.godot`. The pin is therefore an **effective-value assertion** (§ 5.3): CI asserts the effective `ProjectSettings` values (headless-safe); a dev build halts at boot when the live printed driver is not the expected one. A later choice of D3D12 is written explicitly and changes the expected value in one constant.
- **Silent fallback is disabled.** The engine has `rendering/rendering_device/fallback_to_opengl3` (default true), `fallback_to_d3d12` and `fallback_to_vulkan` (both default true). With Vulkan the pin, `fallback_to_opengl3 = false` and `fallback_to_d3d12 = false` are **required keys in `project.godot`** (their defaults are `true`, so they cannot be absent); `fallback_to_vulkan = false` is added if the D3D12 reversal is taken. A failed driver init then errors visibly instead of degrading to Compatibility, where `use_hdr_2d` is ignored, `Light2D` and glow behave differently and the colour path changes (§ 2.2). **A wrong effective driver or method in a release build is a visible fatal "unsupported GPU" screen** (text only: expected and actual method and driver, then exit on any key), written to the diagnostics header as well; it never logs and continues, because a release build that silently ships a different look is the failure this pin exists to prevent.

**Why Forward+.** The Lighting GDD's ambient floor, glow and `hdr_2d` model (steps 7 and 8 of the spike) assume a float 2D framebuffer and the 4.6 glow-before-tonemapping behaviour, and the art bible sets `hdr_2d` for exactly that reason. The claim that `use_hdr_2d` is a Forward+ and Mobile feature is now **CONFIRMED by probe** (Compatibility silently ignores it). At MVP the world viewport is nevertheless SDR (§ 2.2), because an HDR viewport drawn through a container on the SDR root outputs unconverted linear colour; Forward+ is kept for `Light2D` and glow parity with the reference machines and so that the gated HDR contingency of § 2.4 stays open. The reference cost of Forward+ is the Vulkan-class requirement, which both reference machines state (RM-DESKTOP "Vulkan 1.2+", the Deck). Compatibility remains the **reversible fallback** the Lighting GDD keeps open (step 9); a reversal re-opens the glow and ambient design, shader support for the five-material cap, the colour path (the HDR resolve is renderer-specific, § 2.4) and the pass-B figures of § 7, and re-runs the spike, so it is a decision for the technical director, not a settings flip.

**Why Vulkan on Windows.** (a) RM-DESKTOP is specified in Vulkan terms and RM-DECK is Vulkan, so one driver family produces the numbers the budget table is judged on and any driver-specific rendering difference (shader variants, glow, float framebuffers) is found once. (b) The reference gives D3D12's reason as "better driver compatibility", which concerns old and integrated GPUs below the minimum specification; it does not apply to a GTX 1050 Ti or RX 570 class card. (c) The installed binary's built-in default is Vulkan, and a key-absent project reports Vulkan (windowed probe). (d) The D3D12 backend is the newer one (UNVERIFIED stability on 4.7.2); the cost of choosing the older backend is nothing at this tier. **Tie-break rule recorded for the spike:** switch to D3D12 only if lighting spike steps 1 and 2 on RM-DESKTOP show Vulkan failing a correctness check (palette-exact fills, hard cone edge, glow) that D3D12 passes, or D3D12 beating Vulkan's P99 CPU frame time by 10 % or more on the same scene; record both numbers either way. HDR output is off (§ 5), so the one Windows feature that might favour D3D12 is not used at MVP.

**What gates it.** Lighting spike step 1 (print the driver name and rendering method and whether `hdr_2d` is honoured), step 2 (pass A/B), step 9 (Compatibility parity), pipeline spike step 11 and (for the release export) step 12. This section's status is therefore "provisional until those have run", independent of the rest of the ADR.

### 2. The viewport stack and scale wiring (wiring candidate (i), refined)

**Decision.** The root `Window` runs with **stretch disabled**. Every scale in the window is chosen by script and is an integer by construction. One node, the **`PipelineRoot`**, is the only writer of the world viewport's size, override, scale, offset (the world `canvas_transform` is written by the `CameraHost` handler it owns, § 6.2), of every `CanvasLayer` transform, and the only caller of `HudLayout`.

```
root Window  (content_scale_mode = DISABLED, content_scale_factor = 1.0, min_size = 1280x720, clear colour black)
└─ PipelineRoot (Node; process_priority = ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION; the single PresentationHost (ADR-0009 § 3);
   │              owns the PresentationDriver; sole writer of everything below)
   ├─ WorldContainer: SubViewportContainer          layer 0   top-level Control on the root canvas
   │    stretch = false · mouse_filter = IGNORE · mouse_target = false · texture_filter = TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST (1)
   │    position = world_rect.position (integer valued) · scale = (k_z, k_z) under pass A, (1, 1) under pass B
   │    material = null at MVP (the single Filter hook, § 2.4)
   │    └─ WorldViewport: SubViewport                     size, override, SDR, snap, filter: § 2.2
   │         └─ the body frame: floors, Y-sorted layer, caps, lights, occluders, fringe, dust, horrors, web, instruments
   │             (CameraHost's frame_pre_draw handler writes this viewport's canvas_transform, § 6.2)
   ├─ CameraHost: Node                                no geometry; holds the solved pose; its frame_pre_draw handler is the only camera write
   ├─ HoldLayer        CanvasLayer  layer = 1   one opaque #000000 quad, only in TRANSIT_HOLD and BOOTING / LOADING
   ├─ HudLayer         CanvasLayer  layer = 2   group "hud"; scale = (H, H); offset = hud_rect.position
   │    └─ HudRoot: Control, size = hud_rect.size / H (fractional allowed), Control.scale = (1, 1)
   ├─ MenuPixelLayer   CanvasLayer  layer = 3   scale = (H, H)   bitmap-face chart table and menus
   ├─ MenuReadingLayer CanvasLayer  layer = 4   scale = (1, 1)   reading-face text, sizes in screen px (§ 2.5)
   └─ DebugLayer       CanvasLayer  layer = 5   scale = (H, H)   dev builds only; absent from release exports
```

**2.1 Why this wiring (what the probes show).** Root integer stretch gave exactly `(k, k)` with the correct centring offset at every window tried, but only for the **default step with `H` equal to `k`**: its single scale applies to everything under the root, so a HUD at 3x over a 2x world, or a world at `picture / k_z`, would need a second, non-integer multiplier (the double-scale hazard of PR-7, candidate (ii)). With stretch disabled, a `CanvasLayer.scale` of (3,3) gave a child `Control` an exact scale of 3 with the root transform identity, and a `scale` of (3,3) on a `stretch = false` container gave an exact scale of 3; so the Deck's world 2x and HUD 3x are two independent integers chosen from script. `stretch_shrink` floors (3840/7 gives 548) and is an integer divisor of the container size, so candidate (iii) cannot reach `picture / k_z` at every step and is rejected as the primary; it remains the recorded fallback for the default step only (Alternative 2).

**2.2 The world viewport members the root sets explicitly (every value is the probed built-in default's opposite or must not be inherited).**
- `size`: under pass A `field_px` (the logical size in base px, § 3); under pass B `world_rect.size` (`field_px * k_z`). **Never the 512x512 default and never the window size.** A scene that finds `size == (512, 512)` fails the scene-tree lint.
- `size_2d_override` and `size_2d_override_stretch`: unset (0,0) and `false` under pass A; `field_px` and `true` under pass B. **The override must divide the size exactly** (probed: 1366x768 over 682x384 gives a scale of 2.002933), which § 3 guarantees by sizing the viewport as `field_px * k_z`.
- `use_hdr_2d = false` **at MVP** (the world viewport is SDR like the root). Windowed probe: an HDR viewport drawn through a container on the SDR root outputs unconverted linear colour (a flat `(128, 64, 200)` fill reads back `(55, 13, 147)`; the clear colour `(19, 19, 19)` instead of 76), which contradicts the palette-exact-fills goal, the container-material-null rule (§ 2.4) and `filter_route = PER_ELEMENT, slot = NOT_USED`. The flat-palette guarantee therefore holds only with the world SDR. The HDR path is a specified but unbuilt contingency (§ 2.4), adopted only if lighting spike steps 7 and 8 prove the ambient floor and glow cannot be met without it. Never set on the root viewport.
- `canvas_item_default_texture_filter = Viewport.DEFAULT_CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST` (0); `use_debanding = false`; `transparent_bg = false`; `handle_input_locally = false` (the world has no `Control`; the effect of this member under a container that forwards no mouse events is UNVERIFIED, step 11, and the member may be left at its default if it proves irrelevant).
- `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel = true`; `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel = true` (belt and braces). **Probed (pass B, Forward+): the flags snap in base-pixel space, not screen-pixel space**, because `canvas_transform` is in override (base-pixel) units; they round to nearest rather than floor. Under pass A the viewport is the base-pixel field, so the same holds. Nothing relies on them: placement is by integer write (ADR-0009), and `pose_q` and the parallax offsets are still written as integer-valued `Vector2` so rounding and flooring never differ. This answers ADR-0009's question on the flags.
- `render_target_update_mode`: `UPDATE_ALWAYS` in `PRESENTING`, `TRANSIT_HOLD` with something to show and `RESCALING`; `UPDATE_DISABLED` in `PAUSED_FROZEN` and `HIDDEN`. **Probed: any size change while the viewport is `UPDATE_DISABLED` clears its target (Forward+ shows `(0, 0, 0)`, Compatibility the clear colour), so `UPDATE_ONCE` set on the frame of any `RESCALING` that happens while updates are disabled is mandatory, not a guard**; it redraws the target and the result is composited the same frame, so it is also sufficient. The engine does not write the mode back after the one-shot (the property still reads `UPDATE_ONCE`), so `PipelineRoot` sets `UPDATE_DISABLED` itself on the following frame and **`ViewportWiring` tracks the desired mode in its own field and never reads the property back**. Whether a disabled viewport holds its last texture when no resize occurs (the `PAUSED_FROZEN` hold) is UNVERIFIED but likely; step 11 checks both (pause + resize: no black frame; pause alone: frame held).
- **Nearest filtering is set in three places, with two differently numbered enums**: the project default (`default_texture_filter = 0`), the world viewport member above (`Viewport.DEFAULT_CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST`, value 0), and `SubViewportContainer.texture_filter = CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST` (value 1; the probed default is 0 = `PARENT_NODE`, which would inherit and blur the pass-A upscale). Mipmaps are off on every drawn sheet (art bible 8.4). `TileSet.tile_size` is 48x48 and set explicitly on every tile set (checked by ADR-0010's asset and scene lint, § 5.5(b), not at startup).

**2.3 Layers and what is structurally excluded.** The hold plate (1), HUD (2), menus (3 and 4) and debug overlay (5) are `CanvasLayer`s on the **root** viewport; world lights, glow, `CanvasModulate`, the Filter material on the container and the camera transform live in the world viewport or on the container below them and cannot reach them (PR-3, HR-1, HR-6, HR-13). Nothing that must mix with world light may live above layer 0 (it goes in the world); a `Control` found under the world `SubViewport` fails the scene-tree lint, which is a build gate (HUD HS-2). Layers 2 to 5 are **never dimmed, blurred or desaturated** by pause.

**2.4 The single full-screen hook, and the HDR contingency.** The `SubViewportContainer.material` slot is the pipeline's only full-screen hook (PR-10): assigned and nulled **only** by `PipelineRoot.set_filter_material(material: ShaderMaterial)`, colour-writing only (a policy the Filter owns; the pipeline cannot inspect a shader), drawn below every `CanvasLayer`, receiving the world at screen resolution under both passes. **At MVP the slot is null** (the world viewport is SDR, § 2.2) and the pipeline publishes `filter_route = PER_ELEMENT`, `slot = NOT_USED` as a normal state, not an error (TR-pxl-023, TR-percfilter-030). The truth-channel mask route is a VS-A option that this ADR does not pre-build.

**HDR contingency (specified, not built at MVP).** If lighting spike steps 7 and 8 show the ambient floor and glow need a float framebuffer, `use_hdr_2d = true` on the world viewport is adopted by amending this ADR, and the slot then stops being optional: a **mandatory `PipelineRoot`-owned resolve material** (exact linear-to-sRGB per the probed formula in Engine Compatibility, plus a stated clamp or tonemap policy for values above 1.0) is always in the slot. It composes with the Filter **by inclusion**: the Filter's shader includes the same resolve function, so there is one material and one full-screen pass, no second stage; `set_filter_material` refuses a material that lacks the resolve marker while HDR is on. The resolve is **gated on the effective rendering method**: none under Compatibility, which ignores `use_hdr_2d` (the same shader would double-convert, probed `(188, 137, 229)`). Adoption changes `D_filter` to 1 (not 0), makes `filter_route` / `slot` no longer `NOT_USED`, and extends `StartupCheck` with a resolve-present row; the palette read-back test (§ 5.5(d)) then runs against the resolved output on each renderer. Until adoption, `StartupCheck` asserts `use_hdr_2d == false` and `material == null`.

**2.5 Two integer scales and text.** The HUD canvas is `HudRoot`, a `Control` of size `hud_rect.size / H` at the HUD layer's offset; every HUD element anchors to it, `HudLayout` outputs integer HUD-px rectangles relative to it, and `world_to_hud` returns coordinates in its space (PR-12, HUD HS-9). `Control.scale` stays (1,1) on every HUD node and no node animates scale or rotation. **Reading-face text is never drawn under an integer-scaled layer**: the chart table's reading face lives on `MenuReadingLayer` (layer 4, scale (1,1)), whose labels set their font size to `round(base_size * scale_pct * window_scale)` and whose sizes are in screen px, while its pixel-grid face lives on the sibling `MenuPixelLayer` (layer 3, scale `H`). **The two menu layers have distinct indices, so no draw order rests on a tie-break.** (Probed: two same-index siblings draw later-over-earlier, consistent with the sibling index as the sublayer key, which is fragile to reparenting; giving each layer its own index removes the dependency, and the debug layer moves to 5.) The Chart Table's layer budget (`D_L3`) counts both menu layers.

**2.6 One writer, enforced.** Only `PipelineRoot` (and its `ViewportWiring` helper, `src/presentation/pipeline/viewport_wiring.gd`) may write: `SubViewport.size`, `size_2d_override*`, the container's `position`, `scale`, `stretch_shrink` and `material`, any `CanvasLayer.scale` / `offset` / `transform`, `HudRoot.size`; the world viewport's `canvas_transform` and the parallax layer offsets are written only by the **`CameraHost`'s `frame_pre_draw` handler** (§ 6.2). These two are the geometry writers named on ADR-0009's lint allow-list; they are legitimate and do not go through `Placement` (parallax offsets still use `Placement`'s integer helpers). Presentation subscribers (the Filter, Lighting, HUD, Chart Table) call neither; they receive a read-only `RenderLayout` (§ 3) and `world_to_hud`.

### 3. Geometry: `k`, `H`, aspect, zoom, and one `RESCALING` path

**Decision.** All derived geometry is one **pure function**, `RenderLayout.derive(...)`, a `RefCounted` value with no scene-tree dependency, injected where read. It implements the GDD's Formulas D.1 to D.5 and D.14 as written (the GDD owns the formulas; this ADR owns where their outputs go). `PipelineRoot` is the only caller that applies a result.

- **Inputs:** the window pixel size `W x H_w` (physical pixels, never DPI-scaled; `content_scale_factor` stays 1.0), a `DisplaySettings` value (aspect `KEEP | EXPAND`, manual world scale `0` for Auto, HUD scale choice), the current zoom step `k_z`, the static `ZOOM_MIN_K` row table (carried by `RenderTuning`, § 6.1), and the `offered(P_w, P_h)` subset of HUD scales from `HudLayout` (HUD owns the predicate `bottom_row_fit`). `offered_h` is an `Array[int]` that `derive` duplicates on entry, so a caller that mutates it afterwards, or a layout that keeps it, cannot change a result.
- **Outputs (all integers or integer-valued):** `k_auto = floor(min(W/640, H_w/360))` (a window below `min_size` 1280x720 cannot occur on a compliant window manager; if one does, `k_auto` is clamped to the Section G invariant `k_min == 2` and a `WINDOW_BELOW_MIN` diagnostics entry is written, never a `k` of 1 or 0), `k_base` (manual `k` when below Auto, else `k_auto`; a manual `k` below Auto forces `KEEP`), `H` (`H_default = max(k_auto, 3)`, never below 3, in `[H_default, 2 * H_default]` and in `offered`), `field_px` (D.1/D.3 at `k_base`, D.5 at a ladder step), `picture_rect` (the window region that shows the game, centred, integer), `world_rect = field_px * k_z` centred in the picture (a ladder field that does not divide the picture leaves a few black pixels; the HUD does not move), `hud_rect` (**pinned to the `k_base` picture rect**, so a zoom step never moves the HUD), `hud_canvas = hud_rect.size / H`.
- **Letterbox bars** are the root viewport's **clear colour** (`default_clear_color = (0,0,0,1)`, § 5.1), outside every node, so the Filter, the jolt and any `CanvasLayer` cannot touch them. A 1-HUD-px hairline at the picture edge, if the art director adds one, is a layer-1 element excluded from the HUD count (PR-12 resolution).

**3.1 Zoom is a change of logical size, never `Camera2D.zoom`.** The ladder is `[effective_min, k_base + 2]` with `effective_min = ZOOM_MIN_K(k_base, target class)` (default 1 until the spike fills it); `k_z` is persistent, edge-triggered, never held and never saved. `PipelineRoot.request_zoom_step(direction: int)` is the only entry point (the Input Adapter calls it from its `_process`; ADR-0019). A step is accepted when it is inside the ladder, no other step was accepted this frame, and at least `ZOOM_STEP_MIN_INTERVAL` (0.15 s) of **engine process time** has passed since the last accepted step; the interval is a countdown decremented by the `_process` delta divided by `Engine.time_scale` (guarded when the scale is 0) in `PipelineRoot`, so the cooldown is wall-clock even if `time_scale` is not 1 (whether `time_scale` scales `delta` is UNVERIFIED in ADR-0001; the injected monotonic `Clock` of ADR-0010 is an equivalent source and either satisfies the rule), **not** `present_time` (frozen under pause, where zoom must still work) and not any `Time.*` call (forbidden by ADR-0001's clock lint); surplus presses are discarded, not queued, and counted in `diag.zoom_step_rate_limited`. A refused press (beyond either end, or below `ZOOM_MIN_K`, or while the camera is `HELD`) increments `diag.zoom_step_refused` with a reason. Accepting a step sets the layout dirty, so the step is **one `RESCALING` frame and a camera cut**: under pass A `SubViewport.size = field_px(k_z)` and `container.scale = k_z`; under pass B `size = field_px * k_z`, `override = field_px`. Lighting has no zoom handler: every `Light2D` length is in base px and independent of `k_z` under both passes (LO-16), which this wiring honours because the world canvas is never scaled by `Camera2D`.

**3.2 One `RESCALING` path for every cause.** `Window.size_changed`, a zoom step, a display-mode change, a world-scale or HUD-scale or aspect setting change, and `dpi_changed` each **only set a dirty flag** (the same dirty-mark principle as every notification). `PipelineRoot._process` is the single presentation entry point; it does the following **in this fixed order inside one function** (no priority tie, no tree-order dependency):
1. advance `present_time` (§ 6.3);
2. decrement the zoom cooldown (§ 3.1);
3. if the layout is dirty, run `RESCALING` (below);
4. call `driver.frame(delta, present_time)`, which runs ADR-0009's stages in order, `CAMERA_SOLVE` first (§ 6.2).

The re-derivation therefore happens at most once per rendered frame and completes before any presenter of that frame draws (the main loop processes events, then `_process`, then draws), so a continuous drag of the window edge is a sequence of at most one re-derivation per frame converging on the final size (coalescing by frame, not by time). `RESCALING`:
1. computes the new `RenderLayout`;
2. **reallocates the viewport only if `field_px`, `k_z` or the render mode's size changed**; a pure translation (the picture re-centring by a pixel during a drag) moves only the container position and the HUD rect;
3. applies it through `ViewportWiring` (container position and scale, viewport size and override, layer offsets and scales, `HudRoot.size`), calls `HudLayout` once, re-derives the camera limits rectangle consumed by the solver, increments the layout version counter that `PipelineRoot` holds (consumers poll it), and republishes `world_to_hud`'s inputs;
4. sets `UPDATE_ONCE` on the frame of any size change while updates are disabled (**mandatory**, not a guard: a resize of a disabled viewport clears it, § 2.2), then `PipelineRoot` sets `UPDATE_DISABLED` itself on the next frame;
5. enters the `RESCALING` state for that frame and `PRESENTING` (or the held state) on the next.

The re-derivation completes inside the frame and costs at most 4 ms CPU (§ 7). No frame shows a fractional transform because there is none to show: every transform written is integer-valued. Code that runs right after a resize must not read `WorldContainer.size` or mouse rects: the container is a `Control` under a non-`Control` parent, its `size` refreshes from the viewport's minimum size at the next deferred update and is stale until then (drawing is unaffected with `stretch = false`); only `scale` and `position`, which the pipeline itself wrote, are read (§ Implementation Guidelines, Gotchas).

**3.3 The coordinate conversions are `RenderLayout` methods, not re-derived anywhere (TR-pxl-019, TR-pxl-014).**
- `world_to_hud(body_pos: Vector2i, pose_q: Vector2i) -> Vector2i` (the two-argument form is the only form) is the single projection from a body-frame base-px position to HUD-root coordinates, built from `k_z`, `H`, the container's integer origin, the unjolted `pose_q` and the HUD origin (D.14), floored to the HUD grid. No system re-derives it. `pose_q` is the pose the `CAMERA_SOLVE` stage published earlier in the same `_process`, and the HUD stage runs after it (ADR-0009 stage 5 after stage 1), so the HUD never projects frame N's prompts with frame N-1's pose.
- `mouse_to_world_aim(cursor_px: Vector2i, p: Vector2i) -> Vector2` is the open-loop aim mapping (D.14b): `f_q + (cursor_px - picture_centre) / k_z`, with the published look-ahead-free follow pose `f_q`, no look-ahead, no inner-box clamp, no jolt. Because the root has **no stretch**, `Viewport.get_mouse_position()` on the root already returns window pixels and **no inverse `get_final_transform` conversion is needed** (the GDD's leading candidate (i) says so; candidate (ii) would have needed it). `mouse_to_world_view(cursor_px: Vector2i) -> Vector2` is the full unjolted-pose inverse for picking and pings and **must never feed beam aim** (a lint, ADR-0010). The pipeline root's input mapping tests event types, never `device == 0` (4.7 device IDs, ADR-0019).

### 4. Render mode A or B: one constructor argument, A built at MVP

**Decision.** The render mode is `ViewportWiring.Mode { A, B }`, a **constructor argument** of `ViewportWiring` (the composition root passes a default read from one build constant or feature tag), read only inside `ViewportWiring`. It is an argument rather than a `const` read inside the class because a GDScript `const` cannot be varied in a test, and the equivalence test must construct both wirings. **A is the default and the recorded fallback; B is adopted only if the criteria of art bible 8.12 step 2 are met on the named machines. MVP builds pass A only** behind the `ViewportWiring` seam: B is specified here (table below) but its wiring branch and the A/B equivalence test are built only if lighting spike step 2 adopts B. Everything outside `ViewportWiring` sees an identical `RenderLayout` and identical coordinate, sort, camera and HUD contracts in both modes (PR-7); once B exists, a test constructs both wirings from the same input trace and compares the logical outputs. The lint "only `ViewportWiring` branches on `Mode`" is kept.

| | Pass A (default) | Pass B |
|---|---|---|
| `SubViewport.size` | `field_px` (640x360 at the default step) | `field_px * k_z` (the **picture**, never the window) |
| `size_2d_override` / `_stretch` | unset / false | `field_px` / true |
| `WorldContainer` | `scale = (k_z, k_z)`, position = `world_rect.position` | `scale = (1, 1)`, same position |
| Lights, shadows, glow resolve at | base resolution (cone and shadow edges stair-stepped by `k_z` screen px) | window resolution (1 to 2 screen px edges) |
| Lit pixels, 1080p default / `k_z = 1` | 230,400 / 2,073,600 | 2,073,600 / 2,073,600 |
| World render targets, 1080p | at most 3 MB | at most 22 MB |

**Why the viewport is the picture, not the window, under B.** The PR-7 text puts the pass-B viewport "at window size". The probe shows that an override that does not divide the viewport size gives a non-integer scale (1366x768 over 682x384: 2.002933), so under B the viewport must be exactly `field_px * k_z`, with the letterbox and the ladder remainder outside the container where the clear colour is black. This is a refinement of PR-7, returned as a GDD sync item. Under B the rotated horror and web segments rasterise at window resolution off the grid (tolerated for horrors and web only, PR-4 rule 5); the Q = 1/k camera quantum (Open Question 11, not MVP) is `[UNV]` under B. The cost of B at the bottom ladder step equals A's, so any decision that rests on A's saving is made at the default field and zoom-in steps only (D.16). Under pass B `canvas_transform` is in base-pixel (override) units and the `snap_2d_*` flags snap in base-pixel space (probed, § 2.2); the flags snap to base pixels in both passes, which ADR-0009 may cite.

### 6. The presentation host, the camera solve and write, and `present_time`

**6.1 The camera is a pure solver run in the `CAMERA_SOLVE` stage (TR-pxl-010, 011, 012, 013, 015; the formulas D.6 to D.10 are the GDD's).** `CameraSolver` is a `RefCounted` with `solve(input: SolverInput, state: SolverState, params: SolverParams) -> Pose`, no scene-tree dependency, float64 per-axis state held as scalars (not `Vector2`), `dt` clamped to `DT_MAX` (0.05 s). The **type of `SolverInput` is the enforcement of Camera C1**: it carries only the follow target's previous and current body-local positions, `tick_alpha`, the raw local beam aim, the zoom step, `dt`, and cut / rebase flags; it has no field through which Attention, breach, horrors, sound, the graph or sanity could enter, so the same input trace gives the same camera trace in calm, tell and breach by construction. The Perception Filter has no write path to a camera or viewport property (§ 2.6). The camera is a `PresenterDescriptor` registered at `PresentationStage.CAMERA_SOLVE` (stage 1, ADR-0009 § 3): it calls `solve` once per frame from `driver.frame` and **publishes `pose_q`, the follow pose `f_q`, the jolt offset, the parallax offsets and the `world_to_hud` inputs** to `CameraHost` and `RenderLayout` before the Avatar, Filter, HUD and Lighting stages run. Solver parameters (`tau_follow`, `DT_MAX`) and `ZOOM_MIN_K` are the `RenderTuning` table loaded by ADR-0007's pipeline and injected (schema in Key Interfaces). Camera state is never persisted.

*Restore and discontinuity.* The kernel calls `snap_baseline` on every interpolated block on each transition into `RUNNING` (ADR-0001 § 4, ADR-0003), so the first frame after a restore interpolates nothing; that is the **only** restore-continuity mechanism and this ADR adds no owner-side rule. The camera stage additionally **CUTs** the solver (starting with `L = 0` easing in) in its `on_discontinuity(DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE)`, which ADR-0009's driver delivers when `PresentationClock.load_seq` changes (the kernel increments it on every `LOADING → RUNNING` transition, restore and new game, never on `PAUSED` or `SAVING → RUNNING`; ADR-0001 amendment batch). A pod or transit body transfer is a CUT; a weld or detach `BODY_TRANSFER` carrying `frame_delta_px` calls `rebase(frame_delta_px)`, which shifts the follow and history and keeps lag and `L`.

**6.2 The frame model and the hook.** `PipelineRoot` **is** ADR-0009's single `PresentationHost` (closing ADR-0009 OQ-E, OQ-J and OQ-L): no other node hosts the driver, and because every step below runs inside one function, no priority tie and no tree-order dependency exists. The composition root constructs the `PresentationDriver` and injects it; `PipelineRoot` holds it. Its single `_process`, at `ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION`, runs in this fixed order: (1) advance `present_time` (§ 6.3); (2) the zoom cooldown (§ 3.1); (3) the `RESCALING` re-derive if dirty (§ 3.2); (4) `driver.frame(delta, present_time)`, which runs the stages with `CAMERA_SOLVE` first. Presenters have no `_process`; **there are no subscribers drawing from their own `_process`** (ADR-0009 Alternatives 1 and 2 reject that shape).

The `CameraHost` (a top-level presentation node under `PipelineRoot`, never a child of a body) connects one handler to **`RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw`**. The handler does exactly two writes from already-solved values and nothing else: the world viewport's `canvas_transform` (from `pose_q` plus the jolt offset) and the parallax layer offsets (integer offsets the camera stage computed with `Placement`'s integer helpers, `floori`, not a bare `-floor(...)`). It **does not solve**, it is **idempotent and branch-free**, and it is **safe if the handler is skipped for a frame** (a minimised or occluded window): the next call writes the then-current solved values and nothing accumulates. **Primary variant: no `Camera2D` in the world tree** (a lint); the transform has scale (1,1), no rotation and no skew every frame and only the host writes it. **Alternative variant**, if the direct write is rejected at step 12: a `Camera2D` with `anchor_mode = ANCHOR_MODE_FIXED_TOP_LEFT` (probed: `anchor_mode` default 1 is `DRAG_CENTER`), drag margins off, and `force_update_scroll()` called after each write; every camera assertion is read as holding on the `Camera2D` if the variant has one. `Camera2D.limit_*` stays at the engine defaults in both variants; **the solver is the only clamp** against the limits rectangle a PROJECTOR sets (ADR-0034), so `world_to_hud` is never offset while `CLAMPED`. A `Camera2D` never descends from a physics body.

*Why the solve is not in the handler.* Probed ordering (windowed 4.7.2 editor, Forward+, main thread, `thread_model` 1 and 2): all node `_process`, then `frame_pre_draw`, then `frame_post_draw`; a `canvas_transform` written in the handler is the one drawn that frame, and a write from `_process` is also drawn that frame. The handler therefore runs after the HUD stage, so a solve inside it would leave `world_to_hud`, the Avatar presenter's beam pose and `mouse_to_world_aim` one frame behind the world: a permanent HUD-versus-world disagreement on exactly the "screen is still when the ship is still" surface (PR-6 C11, TR-pxl-019). Solving in the `_process` pass also keeps the solver unit-testable without a signal that never fires headless.

*Verification status (TD-20).* Windowed 4.7.2 editor: all node `_process`, then `frame_pre_draw`, then `frame_post_draw` (probed); it fires only when a frame is drawn (never headless). Release export, Direct3D 12, the Steam Deck, a minimised or occluded window and `low_processor_mode` are UNVERIFIED (pipeline spike step 12 re-runs the same probe on a release export). `rendering/driver/threads/thread_model` is pinned at 1 (§ 5.1; value 2 unsupported) so the probed ordering holds. **Fallback, used only if `frame_pre_draw` fails the release-export spike:** the canvas write moves to the last statement of `PipelineRoot._process`, after `driver.frame(...)`. That needs no new `ProcessPriority` constant: `PRESENTATION_LATE` is withdrawn (ADR-0001 keeps three constants plus `HOST_SERVICE`).

*Canvas coordinate exactness (TD-23, E14; ADR-0005 TR-shipbody-038 and ADR-0010 cite this paragraph).* **Presentation coordinates are integer-valued `float32` and exact for `|v| <= 2^24` (16,777,216) base px.** `Transform2D`, `Node2D.position` and `Control.position` are `float32` in the standard build (`Engine.is_double_precision()` was not checked and is assumed false). `pose_q` and every placement are `Vector2i`; a `Vector2i` is converted to `Vector2` **only** at `Placement.put` and at the `canvas_transform` write, and the solver's float64 scalars are quantised to `Vector2i` before that conversion, so that conversion is the one point where exactness is kept. World and body-frame extents stay below 2^24 base px; if body-frame extents could exceed that, ADR-0015 owns the bound (the rebase mechanism of § 6.1 exists to keep body-frame coordinates inside it). A unit test constructs the write at `2^24 - 1`, `2^24` and `2^24 + 1` and asserts the first two round-trip and the third is rejected or rebased, never silently rounded.

*Scope edge with ADR-0009.* The Pipeline GDD PR-8 item 3 calls the pipeline root's `frame_pre_draw` handler the "render callback" in which every subscriber reads and draws. That is **not** adopted: subscribers draw from `driver.frame` in the `_process` pass (ADR-0009 § 3), and `frame_pre_draw` is reserved for the `CameraHost`'s two writes. This is returned as a GDD sync item.

**6.3 `present_time`, the pipeline-owned clock (ADR-0001 handed the owner to this ADR).** `PipelineRoot` owns `present_time: float` (seconds, a 64-bit float). Step (1) of `_process` advances it by the `_process` delta while `PresentationClock.state` is `RUNNING`, `SAVING`, or `LOADING` with the hold shown, and leaves it frozen while `PAUSED`; it is **never scaled by reduced motion** (reduced motion scales individual effects). Layer 0 animation uses only `present_time` (delivered to presenters as `PresentFrame.present_time`); the menu layers (3 and 4) and the debug layer (5) run on engine process time so the chart table responds while paused; the HUD (layer 2) freezes with the world. The cosmetic-phase rule ("the tick counter is never used for cosmetic phase") is ADR-0001's and is not restated. The kernel state comes from the read-only `PresentationClock.state: int` (the kernel state enum: `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `LOADING`, `FAULTED`), and `setup()` takes `PresentationClock` only; no `KernelStateView` type exists. This depends on the ADR-0001 amendment batch (Depends On, Ordering Note). `SceneTree.paused` is not the kernel's pause and is not used by the pipeline.

**6.4 Pipeline states.** The pipeline state machine (`BOOTING`, `PRESENTING`, `RESCALING`, `TRANSIT_HOLD`, `PAUSED_FROZEN`, `HIDDEN`, with the `DEBUG_OVERLAY` modifier) is implemented as the GDD's States and Transitions table, with the camera state as three independent fields (follow, zoom, hold). The wiring-specific rules recorded here: `PAUSED_FROZEN` sets `UPDATE_DISABLED` and holds an undimmed last frame (a resize while paused forces the one-shot `UPDATE_ONCE` of § 2.2, or the held frame would be blank); `TRANSIT_HOLD` shows the layer-1 black quad (`#000000`, no text) with a 120 ms fade in and a cut out; `FAULTED` is not a pipeline state (the pipeline keeps presenting the last committed state; a dev build halts with the overlay); any `(state, trigger)` pair not listed is ignored and reported to diagnostics.

571	## Performance Implications
572	- **CPU**: `PipelineRoot._process` at most 0.5 ms P99 including the state machine and `world_to_hud` for 32 prompts; `CameraSolver.solve` (the `CAMERA_SOLVE` stage) at most 0.05 ms; the `RESCALING` re-derivation at most 4 ms, once per resize frame, with viewport reallocation only when `field_px` or `k_z` changes. All unmeasured until the release-export spike.
573	- **Memory**: world render targets at most 3 MB (A) or 22 MB (B) at 1080p, scaled by lit pixels at other targets (D.16). `RenderLayout` is a handful of integers per rederivation.
574	- **Load Time**: negligible; the pipeline root builds the stack in BOOTING step 2 before content loads. Shader Baker reduces first-frame hitching (measured by lighting spike step 10).
575	- **GPU**: the container composite at most 0.3 ms (1080p) and 1.0 ms (2160p). Pass A shades 230,400 lit pixels at the default field; at the bottom ladder step A costs the same as B (2,073,600 at 1080p).
576	- **Network**: none. Nothing here is replicated; each client has its own window and camera.

87	### 1. Renderer method and Windows driver
88	
89	**Decision (provisional, pinned, spike-reversible).**
90	- **Method: Forward+** (`rendering/renderer/rendering_method = "forward_plus"`, already in `project.godot`). Compatibility and Mobile are assumed nowhere.
91	- **Windows driver: Vulkan** (`rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows = "vulkan"`), and the Linux / Steam Deck driver is Vulkan (`driver.linuxbsd = "vulkan"`). Direct3D 12 is the recorded alternative.
92	- **The driver is never left to the engine default.** Windowed probe on 4.7.2: a project with no driver key reports `vulkan` / `forward_plus`, and the `ProjectSettings` default of `driver.windows` is `vulkan` (`driver.linuxbsd` `vulkan`, `driver.macos` `metal`); the reference's "D3D12 is the Windows default since 4.6" is therefore not what a key-absent project gets and is most plausibly a new-project-template value (UNVERIFIED, OQ-C). Either could be the value a later 4.7.x patch or a template re-save writes, and the editor drops a key whose value equals its default, so the key may be absent from `project.godot`. The pin is therefore an **effective-value assertion** (§ 5.3): CI asserts the effective `ProjectSettings` values (headless-safe); a dev build halts at boot when the live printed driver is not the expected one. A later choice of D3D12 is written explicitly and changes the expected value in one constant.
93	- **Silent fallback is disabled.** The engine has `rendering/rendering_device/fallback_to_opengl3` (default true), `fallback_to_d3d12` and `fallback_to_vulkan` (both default true). With Vulkan the pin, `fallback_to_opengl3 = false` and `fallback_to_d3d12 = false` are **required keys in `project.godot`** (their defaults are `true`, so they cannot be absent); `fallback_to_vulkan = false` is added if the D3D12 reversal is taken. A failed driver init then errors visibly instead of degrading to Compatibility, where `use_hdr_2d` is ignored, `Light2D` and glow behave differently and the colour path changes (§ 2.2). **A wrong effective driver or method in a release build is a visible fatal "unsupported GPU" screen** (text only: expected and actual method and driver, then exit on any key), written to the diagnostics header as well; it never logs and continues, because a release build that silently ships a different look is the failure this pin exists to prevent.
94	
95	**Why Forward+.** The Lighting GDD's ambient floor, glow and `hdr_2d` model (steps 7 and 8 of the spike) assume a float 2D framebuffer and the 4.6 glow-before-tonemapping behaviour, and the art bible sets `hdr_2d` for exactly that reason. The claim that `use_hdr_2d` is a Forward+ and Mobile feature is now **CONFIRMED by probe** (Compatibility silently ignores it). At MVP the world viewport is nevertheless SDR (§ 2.2), because an HDR viewport drawn through a container on the SDR root outputs unconverted linear colour; Forward+ is kept for `Light2D` and glow parity with the reference machines and so that the gated HDR contingency of § 2.4 stays open. The reference cost of Forward+ is the Vulkan-class requirement, which both reference machines state (RM-DESKTOP "Vulkan 1.2+", the Deck). Compatibility remains the **reversible fallback** the Lighting GDD keeps open (step 9); a reversal re-opens the glow and ambient design, shader support for the five-material cap, the colour path (the HDR resolve is renderer-specific, § 2.4) and the pass-B figures of § 7, and re-runs the spike, so it is a decision for the technical director, not a settings flip.
96	
97	**Why Vulkan on Windows.** (a) RM-DESKTOP is specified in Vulkan terms and RM-DECK is Vulkan, so one driver family produces the numbers the budget table is judged on and any driver-specific rendering difference (shader variants, glow, float framebuffers) is found once. (b) The reference gives D3D12's reason as "better driver compatibility", which concerns old and integrated GPUs below the minimum specification; it does not apply to a GTX 1050 Ti or RX 570 class card. (c) The installed binary's built-in default is Vulkan, and a key-absent project reports Vulkan (windowed probe). (d) The D3D12 backend is the newer one (UNVERIFIED stability on 4.7.2); the cost of choosing the older backend is nothing at this tier. **Tie-break rule recorded for the spike:** switch to D3D12 only if lighting spike steps 1 and 2 on RM-DESKTOP show Vulkan failing a correctness check (palette-exact fills, hard cone edge, glow) that D3D12 passes, or D3D12 beating Vulkan's P99 CPU frame time by 10 % or more on the same scene; record both numbers either way. HDR output is off (§ 5), so the one Windows feature that might favour D3D12 is not used at MVP.
98	
99	**What gates it.** Lighting spike step 1 (print the driver name and rendering method and whether `hdr_2d` is honoured), step 2 (pass A/B), step 9 (Compatibility parity), pipeline spike step 11 and (for the release export) step 12. This section's status is therefore "provisional until those have run", independent of the rest of the ADR.

101	### 2. The viewport stack and scale wiring (wiring candidate (i), refined)
102	
103	**Decision.** The root `Window` runs with **stretch disabled**. Every scale in the window is chosen by script and is an integer by construction. One node, the **`PipelineRoot`**, is the only writer of the world viewport's size, override, scale, offset (the world `canvas_transform` is written by the `CameraHost` handler it owns, § 6.2), of every `CanvasLayer` transform, and the only caller of `HudLayout`.
104	
105	```
106	root Window  (content_scale_mode = DISABLED, content_scale_factor = 1.0, min_size = 1280x720, clear colour black)
107	└─ PipelineRoot (Node; process_priority = ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION; the single PresentationHost (ADR-0009 § 3);
108	   │              owns the PresentationDriver; sole writer of everything below)
109	   ├─ WorldContainer: SubViewportContainer          layer 0   top-level Control on the root canvas
110	   │    stretch = false · mouse_filter = IGNORE · mouse_target = false · texture_filter = TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST (1)
111	   │    position = world_rect.position (integer valued) · scale = (k_z, k_z) under pass A, (1, 1) under pass B
112	   │    material = null at MVP (the single Filter hook, § 2.4)
113	   │    └─ WorldViewport: SubViewport                     size, override, SDR, snap, filter: § 2.2
114	   │         └─ the body frame: floors, Y-sorted layer, caps, lights, occluders, fringe, dust, horrors, web, instruments
115	   │             (CameraHost's frame_pre_draw handler writes this viewport's canvas_transform, § 6.2)
116	   ├─ CameraHost: Node                                no geometry; holds the solved pose; its frame_pre_draw handler is the only camera write
117	   ├─ HoldLayer        CanvasLayer  layer = 1   one opaque #000000 quad, only in TRANSIT_HOLD and BOOTING / LOADING
118	   ├─ HudLayer         CanvasLayer  layer = 2   group "hud"; scale = (H, H); offset = hud_rect.position
119	   │    └─ HudRoot: Control, size = hud_rect.size / H (fractional allowed), Control.scale = (1, 1)
120	   ├─ MenuPixelLayer   CanvasLayer  layer = 3   scale = (H, H)   bitmap-face chart table and menus
121	   ├─ MenuReadingLayer CanvasLayer  layer = 4   scale = (1, 1)   reading-face text, sizes in screen px (§ 2.5)
122	   └─ DebugLayer       CanvasLayer  layer = 5   scale = (H, H)   dev builds only; absent from release exports
123	```
124	
125	**2.1 Why this wiring (what the probes show).** Root integer stretch gave exactly `(k, k)` with the correct centring offset at every window tried, but only for the **default step with `H` equal to `k`**: its single scale applies to everything under the root, so a HUD at 3x over a 2x world, or a world at `picture / k_z`, would need a second, non-integer multiplier (the double-scale hazard of PR-7, candidate (ii)). With stretch disabled, a `CanvasLayer.scale` of (3,3) gave a child `Control` an exact scale of 3 with the root transform identity, and a `scale` of (3,3) on a `stretch = false` container gave an exact scale of 3; so the Deck's world 2x and HUD 3x are two independent integers chosen from script. `stretch_shrink` floors (3840/7 gives 548) and is an integer divisor of the container size, so candidate (iii) cannot reach `picture / k_z` at every step and is rejected as the primary; it remains the recorded fallback for the default step only (Alternative 2).
126	
127	**2.2 The world viewport members the root sets explicitly (every value is the probed built-in default's opposite or must not be inherited).**
128	- `size`: under pass A `field_px` (the logical size in base px, § 3); under pass B `world_rect.size` (`field_px * k_z`). **Never the 512x512 default and never the window size.** A scene that finds `size == (512, 512)` fails the scene-tree lint.
129	- `size_2d_override` and `size_2d_override_stretch`: unset (0,0) and `false` under pass A; `field_px` and `true` under pass B. **The override must divide the size exactly** (probed: 1366x768 over 682x384 gives a scale of 2.002933), which § 3 guarantees by sizing the viewport as `field_px * k_z`.
130	- `use_hdr_2d = false` **at MVP** (the world viewport is SDR like the root). Windowed probe: an HDR viewport drawn through a container on the SDR root outputs unconverted linear colour (a flat `(128, 64, 200)` fill reads back `(55, 13, 147)`; the clear colour `(19, 19, 19)` instead of 76), which contradicts the palette-exact-fills goal, the container-material-null rule (§ 2.4) and `filter_route = PER_ELEMENT, slot = NOT_USED`. The flat-palette guarantee therefore holds only with the world SDR. The HDR path is a specified but unbuilt contingency (§ 2.4), adopted only if lighting spike steps 7 and 8 prove the ambient floor and glow cannot be met without it. Never set on the root viewport.
131	- `canvas_item_default_texture_filter = Viewport.DEFAULT_CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST` (0); `use_debanding = false`; `transparent_bg = false`; `handle_input_locally = false` (the world has no `Control`; the effect of this member under a container that forwards no mouse events is UNVERIFIED, step 11, and the member may be left at its default if it proves irrelevant).
132	- `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel = true`; `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel = true` (belt and braces). **Probed (pass B, Forward+): the flags snap in base-pixel space, not screen-pixel space**, because `canvas_transform` is in override (base-pixel) units; they round to nearest rather than floor. Under pass A the viewport is the base-pixel field, so the same holds. Nothing relies on them: placement is by integer write (ADR-0009), and `pose_q` and the parallax offsets are still written as integer-valued `Vector2` so rounding and flooring never differ. This answers ADR-0009's question on the flags.
133	- `render_target_update_mode`: `UPDATE_ALWAYS` in `PRESENTING`, `TRANSIT_HOLD` with something to show and `RESCALING`; `UPDATE_DISABLED` in `PAUSED_FROZEN` and `HIDDEN`. **Probed: any size change while the viewport is `UPDATE_DISABLED` clears its target (Forward+ shows `(0, 0, 0)`, Compatibility the clear colour), so `UPDATE_ONCE` set on the frame of any `RESCALING` that happens while updates are disabled is mandatory, not a guard**; it redraws the target and the result is composited the same frame, so it is also sufficient. The engine does not write the mode back after the one-shot (the property still reads `UPDATE_ONCE`), so `PipelineRoot` sets `UPDATE_DISABLED` itself on the following frame and **`ViewportWiring` tracks the desired mode in its own field and never reads the property back**. Whether a disabled viewport holds its last texture when no resize occurs (the `PAUSED_FROZEN` hold) is UNVERIFIED but likely; step 11 checks both (pause + resize: no black frame; pause alone: frame held).
134	- **Nearest filtering is set in three places, with two differently numbered enums**: the project default (`default_texture_filter = 0`), the world viewport member above (`Viewport.DEFAULT_CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST`, value 0), and `SubViewportContainer.texture_filter = CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST` (value 1; the probed default is 0 = `PARENT_NODE`, which would inherit and blur the pass-A upscale). Mipmaps are off on every drawn sheet (art bible 8.4). `TileSet.tile_size` is 48x48 and set explicitly on every tile set (checked by ADR-0010's asset and scene lint, § 5.5(b), not at startup).
135	
136	**2.3 Layers and what is structurally excluded.** The hold plate (1), HUD (2), menus (3 and 4) and debug overlay (5) are `CanvasLayer`s on the **root** viewport; world lights, glow, `CanvasModulate`, the Filter material on the container and the camera transform live in the world viewport or on the container below them and cannot reach them (PR-3, HR-1, HR-6, HR-13). Nothing that must mix with world light may live above layer 0 (it goes in the world); a `Control` found under the world `SubViewport` fails the scene-tree lint, which is a build gate (HUD HS-2). Layers 2 to 5 are **never dimmed, blurred or desaturated** by pause.
137	
138	**2.4 The single full-screen hook, and the HDR contingency.** The `SubViewportContainer.material` slot is the pipeline's only full-screen hook (PR-10): assigned and nulled **only** by `PipelineRoot.set_filter_material(material: ShaderMaterial)`, colour-writing only (a policy the Filter owns; the pipeline cannot inspect a shader), drawn below every `CanvasLayer`, receiving the world at screen resolution under both passes. **At MVP the slot is null** (the world viewport is SDR, § 2.2) and the pipeline publishes `filter_route = PER_ELEMENT`, `slot = NOT_USED` as a normal state, not an error (TR-pxl-023, TR-percfilter-030). The truth-channel mask route is a VS-A option that this ADR does not pre-build.
139	
140	**HDR contingency (specified, not built at MVP).** If lighting spike steps 7 and 8 show the ambient floor and glow need a float framebuffer, `use_hdr_2d = true` on the world viewport is adopted by amending this ADR, and the slot then stops being optional: a **mandatory `PipelineRoot`-owned resolve material** (exact linear-to-sRGB per the probed formula in Engine Compatibility, plus a stated clamp or tonemap policy for values above 1.0) is always in the slot. It composes with the Filter **by inclusion**: the Filter's shader includes the same resolve function, so there is one material and one full-screen pass, no second stage; `set_filter_material` refuses a material that lacks the resolve marker while HDR is on. The resolve is **gated on the effective rendering method**: none under Compatibility, which ignores `use_hdr_2d` (the same shader would double-convert, probed `(188, 137, 229)`). Adoption changes `D_filter` to 1 (not 0), makes `filter_route` / `slot` no longer `NOT_USED`, and extends `StartupCheck` with a resolve-present row; the palette read-back test (§ 5.5(d)) then runs against the resolved output on each renderer. Until adoption, `StartupCheck` asserts `use_hdr_2d == false` and `material == null`.
141	
142	**2.5 Two integer scales and text.** The HUD canvas is `HudRoot`, a `Control` of size `hud_rect.size / H` at the HUD layer's offset; every HUD element anchors to it, `HudLayout` outputs integer HUD-px rectangles relative to it, and `world_to_hud` returns coordinates in its space (PR-12, HUD HS-9). `Control.scale` stays (1,1) on every HUD node and no node animates scale or rotation. **Reading-face text is never drawn under an integer-scaled layer**: the chart table's reading face lives on `MenuReadingLayer` (layer 4, scale (1,1)), whose labels set their font size to `round(base_size * scale_pct * window_scale)` and whose sizes are in screen px, while its pixel-grid face lives on the sibling `MenuPixelLayer` (layer 3, scale `H`). **The two menu layers have distinct indices, so no draw order rests on a tie-break.** (Probed: two same-index siblings draw later-over-earlier, consistent with the sibling index as the sublayer key, which is fragile to reparenting; giving each layer its own index removes the dependency, and the debug layer moves to 5.) The Chart Table's layer budget (`D_L3`) counts both menu layers.
143	
144	**2.6 One writer, enforced.** Only `PipelineRoot` (and its `ViewportWiring` helper, `src/presentation/pipeline/viewport_wiring.gd`) may write: `SubViewport.size`, `size_2d_override*`, the container's `position`, `scale`, `stretch_shrink` and `material`, any `CanvasLayer.scale` / `offset` / `transform`, `HudRoot.size`; the world viewport's `canvas_transform` and the parallax layer offsets are written only by the **`CameraHost`'s `frame_pre_draw` handler** (§ 6.2). These two are the geometry writers named on ADR-0009's lint allow-list; they are legitimate and do not go through `Placement` (parallax offsets still use `Placement`'s integer helpers). Presentation subscribers (the Filter, Lighting, HUD, Chart Table) call neither; they receive a read-only `RenderLayout` (§ 3) and `world_to_hud`.
145	
146	### 3. Geometry: `k`, `H`, aspect, zoom, and one `RESCALING` path
147	
148	**Decision.** All derived geometry is one **pure function**, `RenderLayout.derive(...)`, a `RefCounted` value with no scene-tree dependency, injected where read. It implements the GDD's Formulas D.1 to D.5 and D.14 as written (the GDD owns the formulas; this ADR owns where their outputs go). `PipelineRoot` is the only caller that applies a result.
149	
150	- **Inputs:** the window pixel size `W x H_w` (physical pixels, never DPI-scaled; `content_scale_factor` stays 1.0), a `DisplaySettings` value (aspect `KEEP | EXPAND`, manual world scale `0` for Auto, HUD scale choice), the current zoom step `k_z`, the static `ZOOM_MIN_K` row table (carried by `RenderTuning`, § 6.1), and the `offered(P_w, P_h)` subset of HUD scales from `HudLayout` (HUD owns the predicate `bottom_row_fit`). `offered_h` is an `Array[int]` that `derive` duplicates on entry, so a caller that mutates it afterwards, or a layout that keeps it, cannot change a result.
151	- **Outputs (all integers or integer-valued):** `k_auto = floor(min(W/640, H_w/360))` (a window below `min_size` 1280x720 cannot occur on a compliant window manager; if one does, `k_auto` is clamped to the Section G invariant `k_min == 2` and a `WINDOW_BELOW_MIN` diagnostics entry is written, never a `k` of 1 or 0), `k_base` (manual `k` when below Auto, else `k_auto`; a manual `k` below Auto forces `KEEP`), `H` (`H_default = max(k_auto, 3)`, never below 3, in `[H_default, 2 * H_default]` and in `offered`), `field_px` (D.1/D.3 at `k_base`, D.5 at a ladder step), `picture_rect` (the window region that shows the game, centred, integer), `world_rect = field_px * k_z` centred in the picture (a ladder field that does not divide the picture leaves a few black pixels; the HUD does not move), `hud_rect` (**pinned to the `k_base` picture rect**, so a zoom step never moves the HUD), `hud_canvas = hud_rect.size / H`.
152	- **Letterbox bars** are the root viewport's **clear colour** (`default_clear_color = (0,0,0,1)`, § 5.1), outside every node, so the Filter, the jolt and any `CanvasLayer` cannot touch them. A 1-HUD-px hairline at the picture edge, if the art director adds one, is a layer-1 element excluded from the HUD count (PR-12 resolution).
153	
154	**3.1 Zoom is a change of logical size, never `Camera2D.zoom`.** The ladder is `[effective_min, k_base + 2]` with `effective_min = ZOOM_MIN_K(k_base, target class)` (default 1 until the spike fills it); `k_z` is persistent, edge-triggered, never held and never saved. `PipelineRoot.request_zoom_step(direction: int)` is the only entry point (the Input Adapter calls it from its `_process`; ADR-0019). A step is accepted when it is inside the ladder, no other step was accepted this frame, and at least `ZOOM_STEP_MIN_INTERVAL` (0.15 s) of **engine process time** has passed since the last accepted step; the interval is a countdown decremented by the `_process` delta divided by `Engine.time_scale` (guarded when the scale is 0) in `PipelineRoot`, so the cooldown is wall-clock even if `time_scale` is not 1 (whether `time_scale` scales `delta` is UNVERIFIED in ADR-0001; the injected monotonic `Clock` of ADR-0010 is an equivalent source and either satisfies the rule), **not** `present_time` (frozen under pause, where zoom must still work) and not any `Time.*` call (forbidden by ADR-0001's clock lint); surplus presses are discarded, not queued, and counted in `diag.zoom_step_rate_limited`. A refused press (beyond either end, or below `ZOOM_MIN_K`, or while the camera is `HELD`) increments `diag.zoom_step_refused` with a reason. Accepting a step sets the layout dirty, so the step is **one `RESCALING` frame and a camera cut**: under pass A `SubViewport.size = field_px(k_z)` and `container.scale = k_z`; under pass B `size = field_px * k_z`, `override = field_px`. Lighting has no zoom handler: every `Light2D` length is in base px and independent of `k_z` under both passes (LO-16), which this wiring honours because the world canvas is never scaled by `Camera2D`.
155	
156	**3.2 One `RESCALING` path for every cause.** `Window.size_changed`, a zoom step, a display-mode change, a world-scale or HUD-scale or aspect setting change, and `dpi_changed` each **only set a dirty flag** (the same dirty-mark principle as every notification). `PipelineRoot._process` is the single presentation entry point; it does the following **in this fixed order inside one function** (no priority tie, no tree-order dependency):
157	1. advance `present_time` (§ 6.3);
158	2. decrement the zoom cooldown (§ 3.1);
159	3. if the layout is dirty, run `RESCALING` (below);
160	4. call `driver.frame(delta, present_time)`, which runs ADR-0009's stages in order, `CAMERA_SOLVE` first (§ 6.2).
161	
162	The re-derivation therefore happens at most once per rendered frame and completes before any presenter of that frame draws (the main loop processes events, then `_process`, then draws), so a continuous drag of the window edge is a sequence of at most one re-derivation per frame converging on the final size (coalescing by frame, not by time). `RESCALING`:
163	1. computes the new `RenderLayout`;
164	2. **reallocates the viewport only if `field_px`, `k_z` or the render mode's size changed**; a pure translation (the picture re-centring by a pixel during a drag) moves only the container position and the HUD rect;
165	3. applies it through `ViewportWiring` (container position and scale, viewport size and override, layer offsets and scales, `HudRoot.size`), calls `HudLayout` once, re-derives the camera limits rectangle consumed by the solver, increments the layout version counter that `PipelineRoot` holds (consumers poll it), and republishes `world_to_hud`'s inputs;
166	4. sets `UPDATE_ONCE` on the frame of any size change while updates are disabled (**mandatory**, not a guard: a resize of a disabled viewport clears it, § 2.2), then `PipelineRoot` sets `UPDATE_DISABLED` itself on the next frame;
167	5. enters the `RESCALING` state for that frame and `PRESENTING` (or the held state) on the next.
168	
169	The re-derivation completes inside the frame and costs at most 4 ms CPU (§ 7). No frame shows a fractional transform because there is none to show: every transform written is integer-valued. Code that runs right after a resize must not read `WorldContainer.size` or mouse rects: the container is a `Control` under a non-`Control` parent, its `size` refreshes from the viewport's minimum size at the next deferred update and is stale until then (drawing is unaffected with `stretch = false`); only `scale` and `position`, which the pipeline itself wrote, are read (§ Implementation Guidelines, Gotchas).
170	
171	**3.3 The coordinate conversions are `RenderLayout` methods, not re-derived anywhere (TR-pxl-019, TR-pxl-014).**
172	- `world_to_hud(body_pos: Vector2i, pose_q: Vector2i) -> Vector2i` (the two-argument form is the only form) is the single projection from a body-frame base-px position to HUD-root coordinates, built from `k_z`, `H`, the container's integer origin, the unjolted `pose_q` and the HUD origin (D.14), floored to the HUD grid. No system re-derives it. `pose_q` is the pose the `CAMERA_SOLVE` stage published earlier in the same `_process`, and the HUD stage runs after it (ADR-0009 stage 5 after stage 1), so the HUD never projects frame N's prompts with frame N-1's pose.
173	- `mouse_to_world_aim(cursor_px: Vector2i, p: Vector2i) -> Vector2` is the open-loop aim mapping (D.14b): `f_q + (cursor_px - picture_centre) / k_z`, with the published look-ahead-free follow pose `f_q`, no look-ahead, no inner-box clamp, no jolt. Because the root has **no stretch**, `Viewport.get_mouse_position()` on the root already returns window pixels and **no inverse `get_final_transform` conversion is needed** (the GDD's leading candidate (i) says so; candidate (ii) would have needed it). `mouse_to_world_view(cursor_px: Vector2i) -> Vector2` is the full unjolted-pose inverse for picking and pings and **must never feed beam aim** (a lint, ADR-0010). The pipeline root's input mapping tests event types, never `device == 0` (4.7 device IDs, ADR-0019).
174	
175	### 4. Render mode A or B: one constructor argument, A built at MVP
176	
177	**Decision.** The render mode is `ViewportWiring.Mode { A, B }`, a **constructor argument** of `ViewportWiring` (the composition root passes a default read from one build constant or feature tag), read only inside `ViewportWiring`.
